name: Check the Payslips: Ladder
description: Ten frozen levels of checking a UK payroll bureau's draft payslips with every rate and rule given in the prompt: the wrong payslips, their six corrected figures to the penny and the employer NI total. Levels 1-2 are one month; from level 3 a level is two to six consecutive months of the same payroll, and every month rests on the ones before it: PAYE is cumulative (each month's tax comes from the correct pay and tax of the earlier months, while the bureau runs on its own wrong year-to-date figures), directors' NI runs on the annual earnings period, K codes catch up tax the 50% limit held back, a coding notice or a move off month 1 changes the code mid-period, a P45 stays in the year-to-date, an apprentice turns 25, and linked sickness serves its waiting days once. The answer includes everyone's taxable pay and tax to date at the end, so one early error spreads. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.
hook: Six months of payslips where every month rests on the last. How far up can it put the whole payroll right?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
From: Gareth Lloyd (Pennine Plumbing & Heating Ltd)
To: you
Subject: November 2026 payroll - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Colne Valley Payroll Bureau have sent the draft payslips for November 2026 (tax month 8, pay day 27 Nov 2026). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for the month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date, rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund).
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Round each employee and employer NI figure to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.

cases.notes: [level 1] 1 month, 4 staff; wrong payslips per month 1; planted E03:sl-rounded-penny. Rules in play: the basics + 2 families (overtime, student-loans). Key = calc() of verification/realworld-business/payroll.mjs month by month along the correct year-to-date chain; second derivation: check_payroll.py recomputes every payslip of every month and the chain independently from payroll-inputs.json. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each with deeper chains of dependent items and more rule families than the one below. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

From: Gareth Lloyd (Pennine Plumbing & Heating Ltd)
To: you
Subject: Payroll October 2026 to December 2026 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Colne Valley Payroll Bureau have sent the draft payslips for October 2026 to December 2026 (tax months 7 to 9; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Round each employee and employer NI figure to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.

From: Priya Raman (Harbour & Hearth Coffee Ltd)
To: you
Subject: Payroll October 2026 to December 2026 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Avon Payroll Services have sent the draft payslips for October 2026 to December 2026 (tax months 7 to 9; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. A starter who joins during the month gets monthly salary x (working days from the start date to the month end) / (working days in the month); working days are Monday to Friday, bank holidays included; rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Hours worked on a Sunday or a bank holiday are overtime at 2x the same hourly rate (not rounded); that overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 2, rounded to the penny. Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice. Pension by salary sacrifice (staff marked so): instead of paying 5% themselves, their pay is reduced by 5% of their qualifying earnings worked out on pay BEFORE that sacrifice (rounded to the penny, half up); the reduction is taken off gross pay before tax, NI and student loan, no employee pension is deducted, and the employer pays 8% of those qualifying earnings.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). Week 1/month 1 (M1) basis: the same with tax month = 1 and no previous pay or tax. BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny. A coding notice from HMRC applies from the payroll it arrives before, on the cumulative basis. New starters: with a P45, use its pay and tax to date as previous figures and its code (cumulative); without a P45, starter checklist statement A: 1257L cumulative, statement B: 1257L M1, statement C: BR.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Company directors use the annual earnings period instead (category A): employee NI to date = 8% of the part of NIable pay to date above £12,570 and up to £50,270, plus 2% of the part above £50,270; employer NI to date = 15% of the part of NIable pay to date above £5,000; this month's NI = NI to date (NIable pay to date before this month plus this month's) minus the NI already paid this tax year, for each of the two. Round each employee and employer NI figure (each NI to date for directors) to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.
Linked sickness. A period of sickness that starts 56 days or less after the last day of the previous period is linked to it: over a run of linked periods the 3 waiting days are served only once (a linked period has only the waiting days the earlier ones did not use; a period that is not linked starts again with 3).

From: Rhiannon Price (Brightsmile Dental Care Ltd)
To: you
Subject: Payroll September 2026 to December 2026 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Soar Payroll Ltd have sent the draft payslips for September 2026 to December 2026 (tax months 6 to 9; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. A starter who joins during the month gets monthly salary x (working days from the start date to the month end) / (working days in the month); working days are Monday to Friday, bank holidays included; rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Hours worked on a Sunday or a bank holiday are overtime at 2x the same hourly rate (not rounded); that overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 2, rounded to the penny. Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice. Pension by salary sacrifice (staff marked so): instead of paying 5% themselves, their pay is reduced by 5% of their qualifying earnings worked out on pay BEFORE that sacrifice (rounded to the penny, half up); the reduction is taken off gross pay before tax, NI and student loan, no employee pension is deducted, and the employer pays 8% of those qualifying earnings.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). Week 1/month 1 (M1) basis: the same with tax month = 1 and no previous pay or tax. BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny. A coding notice from HMRC applies from the payroll it arrives before, on the cumulative basis. New starters: with a P45, use its pay and tax to date as previous figures and its code (cumulative); without a P45, starter checklist statement A: 1257L cumulative, statement B: 1257L M1, statement C: BR.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Company directors use the annual earnings period instead (category A): employee NI to date = 8% of the part of NIable pay to date above £12,570 and up to £50,270, plus 2% of the part above £50,270; employer NI to date = 15% of the part of NIable pay to date above £5,000; this month's NI = NI to date (NIable pay to date before this month plus this month's) minus the NI already paid this tax year, for each of the two. Round each employee and employer NI figure (each NI to date for directors) to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.
Linked sickness. A period of sickness that starts 56 days or less after the last day of the previous period is linked to it: over a run of linked periods the 3 waiting days are served only once (a linked period has only the waiting days the earlier ones did not use; a period that is not linked starts again with 3).

cases.prompt:
From: Gareth Lloyd (Pennine Plumbing & Heating Ltd)
To: you
Subject: Payroll September 2026 to January 2027 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Colne Valley Payroll Bureau have sent the draft payslips for September 2026 to January 2027 (tax months 6 to 10; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. A starter who joins during the month gets monthly salary x (working days from the start date to the month end) / (working days in the month); working days are Monday to Friday, bank holidays included; rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Hours worked on a Sunday or a bank holiday are overtime at 2x the same hourly rate (not rounded); that overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 2, rounded to the penny. Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice. Pension by salary sacrifice (staff marked so): instead of paying 5% themselves, their pay is reduced by 5% of their qualifying earnings worked out on pay BEFORE that sacrifice (rounded to the penny, half up); the reduction is taken off gross pay before tax, NI and student loan, no employee pension is deducted, and the employer pays 8% of those qualifying earnings.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). Week 1/month 1 (M1) basis: the same with tax month = 1 and no previous pay or tax. BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny. A coding notice from HMRC applies from the payroll it arrives before, on the cumulative basis. New starters: with a P45, use its pay and tax to date as previous figures and its code (cumulative); without a P45, starter checklist statement A: 1257L cumulative, statement B: 1257L M1, statement C: BR.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Company directors use the annual earnings period instead (category A): employee NI to date = 8% of the part of NIable pay to date above £12,570 and up to £50,270, plus 2% of the part above £50,270; employer NI to date = 15% of the part of NIable pay to date above £5,000; this month's NI = NI to date (NIable pay to date before this month plus this month's) minus the NI already paid this tax year, for each of the two. Round each employee and employer NI figure (each NI to date for directors) to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.
Linked sickness. A period of sickness that starts 56 days or less after the last day of the previous period is linked to it: over a run of linked periods the 3 waiting days are served only once (a linked period has only the waiting days the earlier ones did not use; a period that is not linked starts again with 3).

cases.prompt:
From: Priya Raman (Harbour & Hearth Coffee Ltd)
To: you
Subject: Payroll August 2026 to December 2026 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Avon Payroll Services have sent the draft payslips for August 2026 to December 2026 (tax months 5 to 9; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. A starter who joins during the month gets monthly salary x (working days from the start date to the month end) / (working days in the month); working days are Monday to Friday, bank holidays included; rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Hours worked on a Sunday or a bank holiday are overtime at 2x the same hourly rate (not rounded); that overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 2, rounded to the penny. Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice. Pension by salary sacrifice (staff marked so): instead of paying 5% themselves, their pay is reduced by 5% of their qualifying earnings worked out on pay BEFORE that sacrifice (rounded to the penny, half up); the reduction is taken off gross pay before tax, NI and student loan, no employee pension is deducted, and the employer pays 8% of those qualifying earnings.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). Week 1/month 1 (M1) basis: the same with tax month = 1 and no previous pay or tax. BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny. A coding notice from HMRC applies from the payroll it arrives before, on the cumulative basis. New starters: with a P45, use its pay and tax to date as previous figures and its code (cumulative); without a P45, starter checklist statement A: 1257L cumulative, statement B: 1257L M1, statement C: BR.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Company directors use the annual earnings period instead (category A): employee NI to date = 8% of the part of NIable pay to date above £12,570 and up to £50,270, plus 2% of the part above £50,270; employer NI to date = 15% of the part of NIable pay to date above £5,000; this month's NI = NI to date (NIable pay to date before this month plus this month's) minus the NI already paid this tax year, for each of the two. Round each employee and employer NI figure (each NI to date for directors) to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.
Linked sickness. A period of sickness that starts 56 days or less after the last day of the previous period is linked to it: over a run of linked periods the 3 waiting days are served only once (a linked period has only the waiting days the earlier ones did not use; a period that is not linked starts again with 3).

Subject: Payroll July 2026 to December 2026 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Soar Payroll Ltd have sent the draft payslips for July 2026 to December 2026 (tax months 4 to 9; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. A starter who joins during the month gets monthly salary x (working days from the start date to the month end) / (working days in the month); working days are Monday to Friday, bank holidays included; rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Hours worked on a Sunday or a bank holiday are overtime at 2x the same hourly rate (not rounded); that overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 2, rounded to the penny. Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice. Pension by salary sacrifice (staff marked so): instead of paying 5% themselves, their pay is reduced by 5% of their qualifying earnings worked out on pay BEFORE that sacrifice (rounded to the penny, half up); the reduction is taken off gross pay before tax, NI and student loan, no employee pension is deducted, and the employer pays 8% of those qualifying earnings.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). Week 1/month 1 (M1) basis: the same with tax month = 1 and no previous pay or tax. BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny. A coding notice from HMRC applies from the payroll it arrives before, on the cumulative basis. New starters: with a P45, use its pay and tax to date as previous figures and its code (cumulative); without a P45, starter checklist statement A: 1257L cumulative, statement B: 1257L M1, statement C: BR.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Company directors use the annual earnings period instead (category A): employee NI to date = 8% of the part of NIable pay to date above £12,570 and up to £50,270, plus 2% of the part above £50,270; employer NI to date = 15% of the part of NIable pay to date above £5,000; this month's NI = NI to date (NIable pay to date before this month plus this month's) minus the NI already paid this tax year, for each of the two. Round each employee and employer NI figure (each NI to date for directors) to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.
Linked sickness. A period of sickness that starts 56 days or less after the last day of the previous period is linked to it: over a run of linked periods the 3 waiting days are served only once (a linked period has only the waiting days the earlier ones did not use; a period that is not linked starts again with 3).

cases.prompt:
From: Gareth Lloyd (Pennine Plumbing & Heating Ltd)
To: you
Subject: Payroll July 2026 to December 2026 - please check the bureau's drafts before I approve the FPS

Hi, Colne Valley Payroll Bureau have sent the draft payslips for July 2026 to December 2026 (tax months 4 to 9; our bookkeeper is off, so nothing has been checked since). Can you check every payslip against the employee records and each month's changes, using the figures below? Tell me which payslips are wrong in each month, what the correct figures are, and the correct employer NI total for each month. Everything you need is in this email.

THIS EXERCISE'S RATES AND RULES (use these exactly; they may differ from HMRC's current figures)
Pay. Monthly salary = annual salary / 12, rounded to the penny (half up). Hourly rate for overtime = annual salary / 52 / contracted weekly hours (not rounded); overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 1.5, rounded to the penny. Hourly-paid staff: hours x rate, rounded to the penny. A starter who joins during the month gets monthly salary x (working days from the start date to the month end) / (working days in the month); working days are Monday to Friday, bank holidays included; rounded to the penny. Unpaid sick day deduction = annual salary x days / 260, rounded to the penny.
SSP (company sick pay is SSP only). SSP is paid at £23.75 a day (£118.75 a week, 5 qualifying days) for qualifying days of sickness after the first 3 qualifying days of a period of sickness (waiting days), and only if average weekly earnings are at least £125.00. The sick days themselves are deducted as unpaid days.
Hours worked on a Sunday or a bank holiday are overtime at 2x the same hourly rate (not rounded); that overtime pay = hours x hourly rate x 2, rounded to the penny. Salary sacrifice (Cycle to Work) is taken off gross pay before tax, NI, pension and student loan. Gross pay on the payslip = pay after salary sacrifice. Pension by salary sacrifice (staff marked so): instead of paying 5% themselves, their pay is reduced by 5% of their qualifying earnings worked out on pay BEFORE that sacrifice (rounded to the penny, half up); the reduction is taken off gross pay before tax, NI and student loan, no employee pension is deducted, and the employer pays 8% of those qualifying earnings.
Pension (auto-enrolment, net pay arrangement). Qualifying earnings for the month = the part of gross pay above £520.00, counting pay only up to £4,189.00 (so: the lower of gross pay and £4,189.00, minus £520.00, never below zero). The employee pays 5% of qualifying earnings and the employer pays 3% of qualifying earnings, each rounded to the penny (half up). Opted-out staff pay nothing. Employee pension is deducted before tax (not before NI or student loan).
Income tax. Taxable pay = gross pay - employee pension. L codes: annual allowance = code number x £10 (1257L = £12,570). K codes: the code number x £10 is ADDED to taxable pay instead. Cumulative basis (normal): allowance to date = annual allowance x tax month / 12 (rounded to the penny); taxable pay to date = previous taxable pay this tax year + this month's taxable pay - allowance to date (K: + the K amount to date), rounded DOWN to the whole pound (never below zero). Bands to date, on taxable pay to date: 20% on the part up to the basic limit (£37,700 x tax month / 12); 40% on the part above the basic limit up to the higher limit (£125,140 x tax month / 12); 45% on the part above the higher limit. Each limit is rounded UP to the whole pound. Tax to date is rounded DOWN to the penny; this month's tax = tax to date - tax already paid this tax year (it can be negative: a refund). Week 1/month 1 (M1) basis: the same with tax month = 1 and no previous pay or tax. BR: 20% of this month's taxable pay; D0: 40% of this month's taxable pay; each rounded down to the penny, with no allowance and no previous pay or tax. K codes: this month's tax may not exceed 50% of this month's taxable pay (the regulatory limit), rounded down to the penny. A coding notice from HMRC applies from the payroll it arrives before, on the cumulative basis. New starters: with a P45, use its pay and tax to date as previous figures and its code (cumulative); without a P45, starter checklist statement A: 1257L cumulative, statement B: 1257L M1, statement C: BR.
National Insurance (monthly, on gross pay). Category A: employee NI = 8% of the part of gross pay above £1,048.00 and up to £4,189.00, plus 2% of the part above £4,189.00; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £417.00. Category C (employee aged 66 or over on pay day): no employee NI; employer as A. Category H (apprentice under 25 on pay day): employee as A; employer NI = 15% of the part of gross pay above £4,189.00 (nothing on pay up to £4,189.00). Use the employee's age on pay day. Company directors use the annual earnings period instead (category A): employee NI to date = 8% of the part of NIable pay to date above £12,570 and up to £50,270, plus 2% of the part above £50,270; employer NI to date = 15% of the part of NIable pay to date above £5,000; this month's NI = NI to date (NIable pay to date before this month plus this month's) minus the NI already paid this tax year, for each of the two. Round each employee and employer NI figure (each NI to date for directors) to the nearest penny, half a penny rounding DOWN.
Student loans (on gross pay, monthly thresholds). Plans 1, 2 and 4 are each deducted at 9% of gross pay above their monthly threshold (Plan 1 £2,172; Plan 2 £2,372; Plan 4 £2,728). The Postgraduate Loan is deducted at 6% of gross pay above £1,750, as well as any plan. Each deduction is rounded DOWN to the whole pound.
Net pay = gross pay - tax - employee NI - employee pension - student loan.
Several months. Work out every month from the CORRECT figures of the months before it: previous taxable pay and tax this tax year are the figures before the first month (from the records or a P45) plus the correct figures of the earlier months below, never the year-to-date figures printed on the bureau's drafts (those are only right if the bureau's earlier payslips were). A director's NI to date works the same way. A coding notice, a starter, a birthday or a sickness takes effect in the month it falls in, and stays in effect for the later months.
Linked sickness. A period of sickness that starts 56 days or less after the last day of the previous period is linked to it: over a run of linked periods the 3 waiting days are served only once (a linked period has only the waiting days the earlier ones did not use; a period that is not linked starts again with 3).
